question: Do the four named primary clinical FAPI sources contain authenticated EMC patient/scan observations that change the R5 shelved paired-imaging conclusion?
hypothesis: At least one presently unassessed subtype roster may authenticate EMC and link to adequate paired FAPI/FDG measurements; this is an eligibility test, not a presumption of advantage.
already_established: R5 evaluated main studies and suitable other rosters; broad sarcoma FAPI uptake and aggregate comparison are already published. No authenticated EMC row retrieved. Standalone paper shelved.
addition_if_success: Complete EMC eligibility and condition evaluation in named missing sources; only authenticated independent paired lesion evidence and a useful, not previously established EMC contrast could justify further analysis.
alternative: Generic sarcoma/chondrosarcoma may be another disease; recycled Essen donors, nonpaired acquisitions, therapy or unverified lesions could explain an apparent advantage.
identity_gate: Explicit extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma or source-supported NR4A3-associated EMC identity, never generic sarcoma, myxoid sarcoma or chondrosarcoma alone.
unchanged_pair_gate: Same patient and lesion; FAPI/FDG scans <=28days and no intervening therapy; comparable acquisition and lesion verification. Evaluate all eligible EMC patients, conditions and unfavorable evidence.
defeat_or_shelve: No authenticated EMC crosswalk, unsuitable chronology/measurements, unresolved eligible coverage, reused single donors without informative comparison, or only previously published disease knowledge: retain shelving, do not compute invented ratios.
